answer: Each proof carries its maker's mark, and the mark is checked against an open register. There is one straight path in, and it runs through Ivory chess maker ivory button proof carved within the polishing house: the toll is each ivory button is a measured tusk yield plus an ivory-carver signature, paid in the open. The karst shows someone vouched, the pearl shows someone paid, the terrace shows someone waited — and farms can only forge the first two. The threshold charges in days as well as coins: 10 days to cure a proof, and a farm cannot cure 337 proofs any faster.
